dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: Good morning. Please, sit down. What brings you in today?

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: Good morning, Doctor. I've had a severe, throbbing pain in my lower left tooth for three days now, and my cheek is noticeably swollen.

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: Let's take a look. Please open wide. Ah, yes, I can see significant inflammation and swelling in the surrounding gum tissue. It appears you have a dental abscess, which is a localized accumulation of pus caused by a bacterial infection.

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: A dental abscess? That sounds alarming. Could that explain why I've also been feeling slightly feverish and having trouble opening my mouth fully?

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: Exactly. A low-grade fever and difficulty opening your mouth are classic signs that the infection is spreading to adjacent tissues. The infection typically originates in the tooth's pulp-usually from deep decay or a micro-crack-and extends down to the root tip.

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: I see. Does this mean the tooth has to be extracted, or can it still be saved?

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: Our main priority is to eliminate the infection while preserving your natural tooth if possible. I'll order a digital X-ray right away to check the condition of the bone and roots. If the structure is intact, we can perform a root canal procedure to clean out the infected tissue and seal the canals.

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: Will I need a prescription for antibiotics as well?

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: Absolutely. Given the facial swelling and your fever, I'll prescribe a course of antibiotics along with anti-inflammatory pain relievers. However, please remember that antibiotics only control the spread-the dental procedure itself is necessary to permanently resolve the issue.

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: Understood. Is there anything I should do to manage this until the procedure?

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: Gently rinse with warm salt water and avoid extreme hot or cold temperatures. Most importantly, if you experience any difficulty breathing or sudden swelling towards your eye or neck, head straight to the emergency department.

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: That makes total sense. Thank you for the clear explanation, Doctor. Let's go ahead with the X-ray.

tests.question: Which of the following is the grammatically and clinically standard question to ask about the duration of symptoms?
